items.title: 56706_Buddy Tate oral history interview
items.q: I saw him fire Paul Gonzales. And I told Paul, I tried to tell him... And he's one of the nicest persons I've ever known

ctx.x: this: You can do anything you want to do. He doesn't get in your business and everything. But when you hit that band-stand, you got to play. Ain't no way in the world he would go through some things like Duke had gone through with some of his guys, no, not with Basie. He'd fire anybody if he comes on his job -- you know, he gave them a chance. But if he's going to drink and keep juicing and interfering with his work, he's not going to be there.

I saw him fire Paul Gonzales. And I told Paul, I tried to tell him, you know, because, see, Paul was the first one, first big -- he worked with us before he went with Diz, then he went with Duke. And he took Illinois' place. And he's one of the nicest persons I've ever known and I used to tell him, he started juicing a little bit heavy and he'd miss -- a couple of times, we were doing theaters and I remember once in Detroit, we got in from Chicago and we had some new acts we had to rehearse and the theater opened…

So Basie says 7:30 and if you go out and hang out with him just because you go out and hang out with him at a bar and get juiced and you go home and go to bed and don't make it, don't think that's going to save you, you know what I mean, because he's going to go there if he had to go sit on
